title: The hash matches. Why do we still not run the file?
goal: Make an admission decision without executing an unknown external processor.

prerequisites.text: Complete P1–P8. Distinguish a common-module function from its application caller; preserve your source and run a separate training infobase.

sections.title: The question we are checking
paragraphs: A card describes unknown.epf: a name and hash are supplied, but no provenance or source code. The correct result is a reasoned decision not to run it. This exercise uses a fictional card; no actual file is required.
Use a new training copy and invented records only. Predict first, then compare the observation; preserve existing functions, files, and records.

sections.title: Practice without executing a file
paragraphs: No BSL module, EPF download or OS-permission change is required. Use only the lesson’s two fictional text cards. H1/H2 denote different bytes; they are not hashes of acquired files.

sections.title: A format is not trust
paragraphs: An external processor is a program component, not a safe table simply because a menu opens it. Specify inputs, modified objects, files, network and output. Use original teaching source. Unknown emailed code must not run on the main computer merely for inspection.

EPF is executable processing and ERF may contain report code. A training filename or screenshot establishes no trust. Use a fictional unknown.epf card, not an actual unknown program: unknown source, known hash, no reviewed source code.

sections.title: A card instead of an executable file
paragraphs: Read the evidence. What is missing for a reasoned admission? A filename and SHA label do not replace source code.

code.source:

Provenance: unknown

No actual file was acquired or opened.

sections.title: Reasoning about the NOT RUN decision
paragraphs: A matching hash establishes only matching bytes. It does not explain who wrote the program, its dependencies, or its permissions. The example therefore ends with NOT RUN and a safe alternative: your known internal report. This is a review decision, not an executed data processor’s output.
The result below is a card-review decision, not program output. No unknown code was executed.

code.source:
Check provenance, source and required permissions.
Necessary evidence is absent → NOT RUN.
Alternative: your own internal training report.

tables.caption: Reasoning about the worked observation
rows: Own internal report — Learning result without unknown code.

sections.title: Bind review to exact bytes
paragraphs: Source review, hash and version form provenance. Changed bytes need new review. Signatures and trusted sources help establish origin but do not replace authority analysis. Embed no secrets and collect no real diagnostic data; synthetic inputs should reproduce the issue.

SHA establishes byte identity, not safety. Record origin, distribution rights, source/dependencies, platform version, required privileges and file/network effects. Missing required information leaves the file NOT RUN.

sections.title: Your prediction first
paragraphs: May an unknown EPF be opened merely to check a matching hash?
Identify the changed action and what should remain unchanged. Reveal the explanation after making your own prediction.

reveal.title: Check the reasoning
paragraphs: No. The card lacks required admission evidence. A copied infobase protects original training data; it does not turn untrusted code into an isolated program.

sections.title: Safe mode has scope
paragraphs: Safe mode constrains specific capabilities in supported contexts; it does not prove full isolation of arbitrary configurations or the host. Rights, server security profiles andVMsare distinct. Choose an execution boundary for the actual threat and test denied actions in a permitted isolated stand.

An infobase copy protects original training data but the 1C process retains OS-user privileges. It is insufficient isolation for untrusted code. Optional engineering Sandbox also does not replace review or licensing.

sections.title: Trace the decision
paragraphs: This diagram records a decision, not execution or a SafeMode simulation. No unknown file was acquired or executed. A complete set of evidence still requires an admission decision before any execution.
Read each step: what is established, what remains unknown, and why is NOT RUN justified?

sections.title: An error that can look successful
paragraphs: “A file with the same name” and “a file whose exact bytes were reviewed” are different claims. A known author does not transfer an older review to modified source or an unreviewed dependency.
Keep the faulty copy separate. To establish a fix, compare the relevant observation with your prior expectation; do not change an expectation merely to obtain a match.

sections.title: Verification must not introduce risk
paragraphs: Inspect source without execution first. After admission, run a new synthetic copy under limits and reconcile effects. Test secret isolation with a synthetic canary, not real secrets. If isolation is unavailable, recordNOTRUN; successfulBSLLSanalysis is not execution.

Use the own internal report instead. For an own EPF retain reviewed source and test only admitted code in a separate copy, recording exact admission and actual execution. This does not authorize arbitrary external processors.

sections.title: Now a new independent task
paragraphs: Review a new fictional card: the author is known, the reviewed version has hash H1, the offered version has H2, and an additional dependency was not supplied for review. Record a decision, two separate reasons, evidence required before reconsideration, and a safe alternative. Download or open no EPF/ERF. Enter NOT RUN and your reasoning in the self-report field: here it records review rather than execution.
First record your decision and two independent reasons. Then reveal the reference for comparison; it does not replace your response.

sections.title: Where to complete this task
paragraphs: Stay on this page. Record the decision, reasons and safe alternative in the self-check explanation field. In the practice self-report explicitly state NOT RUN: there was no external execution.

sections.title: Limits of the observation and your explanation
paragraphs: Only a reasoned review of fictional cards is established here. No platform execution, isolation, blocked access or real-file safety is claimed. A saved response does not establish learner understanding.
Explain the limits of a hash, an infobase copy, and a self-report. Executing unknown code is not required to complete this task.

selfcheck.feedback: The answer is not graded automatically. Compare the reasoning with concrete observations from your work.
